title: Module strict transform commutes with flat source and base pullback
statement: Let $f:X\to S$, $e:T\to S$, $g:Y\to T$, and $j:Y\to X$ be morphisms of schemes with $fj=eg$ [def-pc-scheme]. Assume $e$ and $j$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_S$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent], let $b:S^b=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}S\to S$ and $T^b=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_T}T$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], and identify $T^b\cong T\times_SS^b$ by the flat base-change comparison $\operatorname{bc}_e$ [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map], which is an isomorphism by [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change]. Write $j^b:Y\times_TT^b\to X\times_SS^b$ for the induced morphism [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$, there is a canonical isomorphism $(j^b)^*(\mathcal F^b)\cong(j^*\mathcal F)^{T^b}$ commuting with the quotient maps from the ordinary pullbacks. Here both superscripts mean module strict transform for the specified ideals [def-trf-module-strict-transform], and $j^*$ and $(j^b)^*$ are ordinary module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-blowup-square-pullback-quotient-data] to the given square and $\mathcal F$. Its $B,B_T,P,Q$ are the specified $S^b,T^b,X\times_SS^b,Y\times_TT^b$. Its $u$ has projections $jr$ and $\beta s$, exactly those defining $j^b$; the uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product] therefore gives $u=j^b$. It supplies flatness of $u$, locally principal $D$, $D_Q=u^{-1}D$, quasi-coherent $H,K,H_Q,K_Q$, quotient maps $\pi:H\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F^b$ and $\pi_Q:H_Q\twoheadrightarrow(j^*\mathcal F)^{T^b}$, and the canonical $\gamma:u^*H\cong H_Q$ from $pu=jr$.

source.place: Tag 0805, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up; Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform (1); Tag 02OS, lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor. Extracted geometric and quotient-presentation argument of the returned parent proof steps 1, 2 and 3(a)-(b).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-supported-kernel-flat-pullback] to $u:Q\to P$, $H$ and $D$ from Step 1; all its hypotheses are supplied there. It identifies $u^*(K\hookrightarrow H)$ with the inclusion of the sections of $u^*H$ vanishing off $D_Q$. Since $\gamma$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves, it commutes with restriction to every open, so carries that subsheaf exactly to $K_Q$. Thus $\gamma\circ u^*(K\hookrightarrow H)$ is injective with image $K_Q$.

source.place: Tag 07ZP, lemma-sections-supported-on-closed-subset (2)-(3); compare divisors.tex Tag 080F, lemma-strict-transform-flat, affine power-torsion calculation. The flat-pullback comparison is the agent argument of the returned parent proof step 3(c)-(f).

proof.text: By [def-pc-module-pullback], $u^*$ is left adjoint to $u_*$. Consequently $u^*\pi$ is the cokernel of $u^*(K\hookrightarrow H)$: a map out of $u^*H$ annihilates this inclusion exactly when its adjoint out of $H$ annihilates $K$, hence factors uniquely through $\pi$; adjointing back gives the required unique factorization. By Step 2 the map $\pi_Q\gamma$ is another cokernel of the same arrow, since $\pi_Q$ is the quotient by $K_Q$. Their universal properties give a unique isomorphism $\theta:u^*\mathcal F^b\xrightarrow{\sim}(j^*\mathcal F)^{T^b}$ with $\theta\circ u^*\pi=\pi_Q\circ\gamma$: the factor maps in the two directions are inverse because their composites agree with the identity after the respective quotient epimorphisms. This equation is precisely compatibility with the ordinary-pullback quotient maps. The epimorphism $u^*\pi$ also gives uniqueness, so the isomorphism is canonical.
